question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

When my calculations are wrong, I have to pore over the spreadsheet to find the error.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "have + to + V1 (base form)" expresses obligation/necessity, so "I have to pore over the spreadsheet" is already correct.

• "Pore over" is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to read or study something very carefully and attentively. (ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़ना / गहराई से अध्ययन करना)

◦ Correct: When my calculations are wrong, I have to pore over the spreadsheet to find the error.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "to poring over" is wrong — after the infinitive marker "to" (of "have to"), a gerund (V-ing) cannot be used.

• Option 3 "to pored over" wrongly uses the past form (V2) after "to".

• Option 4 "to pore by" changes the particle; "pore by" is not an English phrasal verb — the correct particles are "over" or "through".

NOTE

• Related phrasal verbs: pore over (study closely), go over (revise/check), look into (investigate), run through (check quickly).

• Do not confuse the verb "pore" (to study) with the noun "pore" (a tiny opening in the skin) or the verb "pour" (to make a liquid flow).

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Jaded
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Fatigued.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Jaded" means tired, worn out or bored, especially after having had too much of something. Its closest synonym is "fatigued" (extremely tired/exhausted). (थका हुआ / ऊबा हुआ)

◦ Example: After twelve hours of travel the jaded/fatigued passengers barely spoke.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Weariless" means never getting tired; tireless — an antonym.

• Option 2 "Unwearied" also means not tired; fresh — again an antonym.

• Option 3 "Beguiled" means charmed, tricked or deceived, which is unrelated to tiredness.

NOTE

• Synonyms of jaded: fatigued, exhausted, weary, worn out, spent, sapped.

• Antonyms of jaded: fresh, energetic, enthusiastic, tireless, unwearied.

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

Are you kidding?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. joking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kidding" means speaking in fun; teasing or joking with somebody. Its exact synonym is "joking". (मज़ाक करना)

◦ Example: "Are you kidding?" = "Are you joking?" — i.e., are you being serious or just having fun?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "rocking" means moving gently to and fro (or, informally, being excellent) — not "joking".

• Option 2 "mixing" means combining/blending things.

• Option 3 "pleading" means begging or making an earnest appeal.

NOTE

• Common expressions with "kid": "Just kidding" (I am only joking), "No kidding!" (really? / seriously), "kid around" (behave playfully).

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

The pillar of light has faded.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. painted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Faded" means lost its colour, brightness or freshness. (रंग/चमक फीका पड़ जाना)

• As per the official answer key, the word taken as its opposite here is "painted" — a surface that is painted is freshly and brightly coloured, i.e., the very reverse of one whose colour has faded.

◦ Example: The old wall had faded, so we had it painted again in bright colours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "melted" (turned into liquid by heat) and Option 4 "vanished" (disappeared completely) are close to the sense of fading away, so they are synonyms, not antonyms.

• Option 1 "grown" means "increased in size" and is not an accepted antonym of "faded" in the colour/brightness sense that this question tests.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fade: dim, dull, wither, pale, wane, die away, vanish.

• Antonyms (colour/brightness sense): brighten, colour, paint, freshen, revive.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The sun was shining through the window.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The sun" is a singular subject, so it takes the singular auxiliary "was"; and the past continuous tense (was + V-ing) correctly shows an action going on at a point of time in the past.

◦ Correct: The sun was shining through the window.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "was shines" is wrong — after "was" we need the -ing form, never the "-s" form of the verb.

• Option 3 "were shined" is wrong on two counts: "were" does not agree with the singular "sun", and "shine" is used here intransitively (it takes no passive).

• Option 4 "were shining" wrongly uses the plural auxiliary "were" with the singular subject "the sun".

NOTE

• Past continuous: was/were + V-ing. Use "was" with I/he/she/it/singular nouns and "were" with we/you/they/plural nouns.

• The verb forms are: shine – shone – shone (to give out light) and shine – shined – shined (to polish, e.g., "He shined his shoes").

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

(Democrats control neither Congress and neither the White House, but) they are doing their best to control the judicial processes.
option_1: Democrat controls neither Congress and nor the White House, though
option_3: Democrats control neither Congress nor the White House, but
option_4: Democrats control neither Congress or the White House, but
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Democrats control neither Congress nor the White House, but.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Neither" must always be paired with "nor" — the correlative pair is "neither ... nor". The bracketed part wrongly uses "neither ... and neither".

◦ Correct: Democrats control neither Congress nor the White House, but they are doing their best to control the judicial processes.

• The two items joined ("Congress" and "the White House") are parallel noun phrases, which is exactly what "neither ... nor" requires.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 uses "neither ... and nor" (wrong pairing) and also changes the plural subject "Democrats" to the singular "Democrat controls".

• Option 2 "No substitution required" is wrong because the printed segment is clearly ungrammatical.

• Option 4 uses "neither ... or", which is an incorrect pairing.

NOTE

• Correlative conjunctions: neither ... nor, either ... or, not only ... but also, both ... and, whether ... or.

• In "neither A nor B", the verb agrees with the nearer subject: "Neither the boys nor the teacher was present.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Shivam is more cleverer than any other boy in the office.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Shivam is more cleverer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cleverer" is already the comparative degree of "clever". Adding "more" before it creates a double comparative, which is always wrong.

◦ Correct: Shivam is cleverer than any other boy in the office.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "than any other boy" is correct — with the comparative degree, we use "than any other + singular noun".

• "in the office." is a correct prepositional phrase.

• Since a clear error exists, Option 4 "No error" cannot be chosen.

NOTE

• Never use more/most with adjectives that already carry -er/-est: "more better", "most best", "more cleverer", "most wisest" are all incorrect.

• Degrees: clever – cleverer – cleverest (also acceptable: clever – more clever – most clever, but never both together).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

A national holiday ______ on the same day as my birthday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. falls.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When we speak of a date or festival occurring on a particular day, the correct verb is "fall on" — "to happen or occur on a particular day/date". (किसी दिन पड़ना)

◦ Correct: A national holiday falls on the same day as my birthday.

◦ Example: Diwali falls on a different date every year.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "false" is an adjective (not true), not a verb, so it cannot follow the subject here.

• Option 3 "flows" is used for liquids or traffic moving smoothly, not for dates.

• Option 4 "fouls" means to make something dirty or to commit a foul in a game.

NOTE

• Useful collocations with "fall": fall on (a date), fall ill/sick, fall short of, fall through (fail), fall back on (rely on).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

That remark ______ a stir.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. created.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Create a stir" is the standard collocation, meaning to cause excitement, commotion or a lot of public interest/controversy. (हलचल मचाना)

◦ Correct: That remark created a stir.

◦ Example: The minister's statement created a stir in Parliament.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "built" and 2 "constructed" are used for physical things (a house, a bridge) or abstractions like confidence and arguments — not with "a stir".

• Option 3 "produced" is used for manufacturing goods, films or results; "produced a stir" is not idiomatic English.

NOTE

• Similar expressions: "cause a stir", "create a sensation", "raise eyebrows", "make waves" — all mean to attract attention or provoke reaction.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Walk on air
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To be extremely happy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "walk on air" means to feel extremely happy, elated or thrilled. (बहुत खुश होना / फूले न समाना)

◦ Example: Ever since she cleared the SSC exam, she has been walking on air.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To work hard" would be "burn the midnight oil" or "sweat blood".

• Option 2 "To describe an unusual situation" does not correspond to any part of this idiom.

• Option 4 "Feeling weakened or tired" is close to the meaning of "run out of steam" or "be worn out" — the opposite of this idiom.

NOTE

• Idioms of happiness: on cloud nine, over the moon, in seventh heaven, on top of the world, walking on air, jump for joy.

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: A few exemples can illustrate this.
option_2: A few examples can illustrate this.
option_3: A few examples can ilustrate this.
option_4: A few examples can illustrrate this.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A few examples can illustrate this.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt words are "examples" (E-X-A-M-P-L-E-S) and "illustrate" (I-L-L-U-S-T-R-A-T-E — double "l" at the beginning, single "r").

◦ Correct: A few examples can illustrate this.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 misspells "examples" as "exemples".

• Option 3 misspells "illustrate" as "ilustrate" (single "l").

• Option 4 misspells "illustrate" as "illustrrate" (double "r").

NOTE

• "Illustrate" means to explain something by giving examples, pictures or diagrams. Related words: illustration (an example/a picture), illustrative, illustrator.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Wet behind the ears
option_1: A sudden change in fortune due to a windfall
option_3: To be young and without experience
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To be young and without experience.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "wet behind the ears" means young, naive and inexperienced — like a newborn animal that is still damp behind the ears. (अनुभवहीन / नौसिखिया)

◦ Example: The new trainee is still wet behind the ears, so guide him patiently.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 relate to luck and betting and have no connection with this idiom.

• The opposite idea is expressed by "an old hand", "a seasoned campaigner" or "dry behind the ears".

NOTE

• Similar idioms for inexperience: a greenhorn, a raw recruit, still in nappies, a babe in the woods, green (as grass).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'

We talked about writing a will, but it / was one of the best thing you never get / around to doing.
option_1: We talked about writing a will, but it
option_2: was one of the best thing you never get
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. was one of the best thing you never get.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "one of the + superlative + plural noun" always takes a plural noun. Hence "one of the best thing" is wrong; it must be "one of the best things".

◦ Correct: We talked about writing a will, but it was one of the best things you never get around to doing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "We talked about writing a will, but it" is correct — "talk about + V-ing" is the right pattern.

• "around to doing." is correct — "get around to doing something" is a phrasal verb meaning to finally find time to do it.

• Since a definite error exists, Option 4 "No Error" is not applicable.

NOTE

• Remember the rule: one of + the + plural noun + singular verb — "One of the best books is missing." The noun is plural, the verb is singular.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'

If Tom was here, / he could have / solved the issue.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. If Tom was here,.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is an unreal/imaginary condition, so the subjunctive form "were" must be used for all subjects after "if", not "was".

◦ Correct: If Tom were here, he could have solved the issue.

• The rule: If + subject + were + ... , subject + would/could/might + verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "he could have" and "solved the issue." are correct as printed — "could have solved" is a proper perfect modal.

• As the sentence does contain an error, Option 3 "No Error" cannot be selected.

NOTE

• Subjunctive "were" is used in unreal conditions and wishes: "If I were you...", "I wish I were taller", "He talks as if he were the boss.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

To ______ your self-worth, write down some things that are positive about yourself.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. affirm.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Affirm" means to state something positively; to confirm or assert the validity of something. Writing down positive things about yourself affirms (confirms and strengthens) your self-worth. (पुष्टि करना / दृढ़ता से कहना)

◦ Correct: To affirm your self-worth, write down some things that are positive about yourself.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "sanctify" means to make holy or sacred, which does not suit self-worth.

• Option 2 "overlook" means to ignore or fail to notice — the opposite of the intended sense.

• Option 4 "repudiate" means to reject or deny — again the opposite of what the sentence needs.

NOTE

• Word family: affirm (verb), affirmation (noun), affirmative (adjective). Synonyms: assert, confirm, declare, uphold. Antonyms: deny, repudiate, negate.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A person who easily believes without demanding proof
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Credulous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Credulous" describes a person who is too ready to believe things without asking for proof; gullible. (भोला / जल्दी विश्वास कर लेने वाला)

◦ Example: The credulous villagers believed the fake godman without question.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Cosmopolitan" means familiar with and at ease in many different countries and cultures.

• Option 3 "Streetwise" means experienced in dealing with the difficulties of city life; shrewd.

• Option 4 "Wary" means cautious and suspicious — the exact opposite of credulous.

NOTE

• Do not confuse credulous (a person who believes too easily) with credible (believable/trustworthy) and creditable (deserving praise). All come from Latin "credere" (to believe).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Ram is ______ like the kings before him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. not.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To make a simple negative statement with the verb "is", the adverb "not" is used: "is not". The sentence means that Ram is unlike the earlier kings.

◦ Correct: Ram is not like the kings before him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "none" is a pronoun (not one/not any) and cannot modify the phrase "like the kings".

• Option 3 "nor" is a conjunction used only with "neither" or after a negative clause.

• Option 4 "no" is a determiner used directly before a noun ("no king", "no time"), not before the preposition "like".

NOTE

• Remember the difference: "no" + noun (There is no water), "not" + verb/adjective/adverb (It is not cold), "none" as a standalone pronoun (None of them came).

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Fear of heights
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Acrophobia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Acrophobia" is the extreme or irrational fear of heights. It comes from the Greek "akron" (peak/height) + "phobos" (fear). (ऊँचाई का डर)

◦ Example: His acrophobia made it impossible for him to look down from the terrace.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Hydrophobia" — fear of water (also a term used for rabies).

• Option 3 "Bathophobia" — fear of depth (deep places, deep water).

• Option 4 "Vaccinophobia" — fear of vaccines/vaccination.

NOTE

• Other common phobias: claustrophobia (closed spaces), agoraphobia (open/public places), xenophobia (foreigners), nyctophobia (darkness), arachnophobia (spiders), pyrophobia (fire).

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Abstract
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Concrete.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Abstract" means existing only as an idea; not physical or tangible. Its antonym is "concrete", meaning definite, specific and existing in a physical form. (अमूर्त का विलोम — मूर्त / ठोस)

◦ Example: Instead of abstract promises, the minister gave concrete proposals.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Transcend" means to go beyond the limits of something — a verb, and not an opposite of "abstract".

• Option 2 "Romantic" relates to love or to an idealised, imaginative outlook.

• Option 3 "Utopian" means idealistic and impractical, which is closer in spirit to "abstract" than opposite to it.

NOTE

• Grammar link: abstract nouns name ideas and qualities (honesty, beauty, freedom), while concrete nouns name things perceived by the senses (table, water, dog).

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Jutsice.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Jutsice" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Justice" (J-U-S-T-I-C-E), meaning fairness; the quality of being just, or the administration of law. (न्याय)

◦ Example: The court delivered justice to the victims.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Blast" (a sudden strong gust or an explosion), "Caste" (a hereditary social class) and "Toast" (grilled bread, or a tribute drunk to someone) are all spelt correctly.

NOTE

• Word family: just (adjective — fair), justice (noun), justify (verb — to show something is right), justification (noun). Also note injustice (the opposite of justice).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

One afternoon, a dozen Arizona State University students (1) ______ to spend the morning cutting cardboard, taping fans and assembling filters in an effort to (2) ______ 125 portable air purifiers for local schools. That (3) ______ morning, staff members at a homeless shelter in Los Angeles were setting (4) ______ 20 homemade purifiers of their own, while in Brookline, Massachusetts, another DIY air purifier was whirring quietly in the back of a day care (5)______ as children played.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. gathered.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gathered" means came together / assembled in one place. A dozen students coming together to spend the morning working on purifiers were said to have "gathered". (इकट्ठा होना)

◦ Correct: One afternoon, a dozen Arizona State University students gathered to spend the morning cutting cardboard ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "plated" means covered with a thin layer of metal or served food on a plate — irrelevant here.

• Option 3 "triggered" means set off or caused something to start, and needs an object.

• Option 4 "dismissed" means sent away or rejected, which contradicts the students getting together to work.

NOTE

• "Gather" collocations: gather round, gather together, gather momentum, gather information, a gathering (a meeting of people).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

One afternoon, a dozen Arizona State University students (1) ______ to spend the morning cutting cardboard, taping fans and assembling filters in an effort to (2) ______ 125 portable air purifiers for local schools. That (3) ______ morning, staff members at a homeless shelter in Los Angeles were setting (4) ______ 20 homemade purifiers of their own, while in Brookline, Massachusetts, another DIY air purifier was whirring quietly in the back of a day care (5)______ as children played.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. build.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Build" means to make or construct something by putting parts together. The students were cutting cardboard, taping fans and assembling filters in order to build 125 portable air purifiers. (बनाना / निर्मित करना)

◦ Correct: ... in an effort to build 125 portable air purifiers for local schools.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "beat" means to strike repeatedly or to defeat.

• Option 3 "sieve" means to pass something through a strainer to separate particles.

• Option 4 "weld" means to join metal pieces by heating — the purifiers here are made of cardboard, tape, fans and filters, not welded metal.

NOTE

• Note the base form "build" after the infinitive marker "to" ("in an effort to build"). Forms: build – built – built.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

One afternoon, a dozen Arizona State University students (1) ______ to spend the morning cutting cardboard, taping fans and assembling filters in an effort to (2) ______ 125 portable air purifiers for local schools. That (3) ______ morning, staff members at a homeless shelter in Los Angeles were setting (4) ______ 20 homemade purifiers of their own, while in Brookline, Massachusetts, another DIY air purifier was whirring quietly in the back of a day care (5)______ as children played.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. same.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is describing events happening simultaneously in different places, so the phrase required is "that same morning", meaning on the very same morning. (उसी सुबह)

◦ Correct: That same morning, staff members at a homeless shelter in Los Angeles were setting up 20 homemade purifiers of their own ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "copy" is a noun/verb and cannot modify "morning".

• Option 2 "cruel" (unkind, causing pain) makes no sense with "morning" in this context.

• Option 3 "resembling" (looking like) is a participle that cannot be placed between "that" and "morning".

NOTE

• "That same + noun" is a common way of stressing that two events occurred at exactly the same time: "that same day", "that same evening", "that very moment".

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

One afternoon, a dozen Arizona State University students (1) ______ to spend the morning cutting cardboard, taping fans and assembling filters in an effort to (2) ______ 125 portable air purifiers for local schools. That (3) ______ morning, staff members at a homeless shelter in Los Angeles were setting (4) ______ 20 homemade purifiers of their own, while in Brookline, Massachusetts, another DIY air purifier was whirring quietly in the back of a day care (5)______ as children played.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. up.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "set up" means to install, assemble or put something in position ready for use. The staff members were setting up 20 homemade purifiers. (स्थापित करना / लगाना)

◦ Correct: ... staff members at a homeless shelter in Los Angeles were setting up 20 homemade purifiers of their own ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Set on" means to attack or urge someone to attack.

• "Set in" means (of something unpleasant) to begin and seem likely to continue — "the rains have set in".

• "Set off" means to start a journey, or to cause something (like an alarm) to go off.

NOTE

• More "set" phrasal verbs: set about (start doing), set aside (keep for later), set out (begin a journey / state clearly), set back (delay), set down (write/record).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

One afternoon, a dozen Arizona State University students (1) ______ to spend the morning cutting cardboard, taping fans and assembling filters in an effort to (2) ______ 125 portable air purifiers for local schools. That (3) ______ morning, staff members at a homeless shelter in Los Angeles were setting (4) ______ 20 homemade purifiers of their own, while in Brookline, Massachusetts, another DIY air purifier was whirring quietly in the back of a day care (5)______ as children played.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. classroom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The purifier was whirring "in the back of a day care classroom as children played". A classroom is a room in which a class of children is taught, and it is the only option that fits a day care centre with children playing. (कक्षा-कक्ष)

◦ Correct: ... another DIY air purifier was whirring quietly in the back of a day care classroom as children played.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "auditorium" is a large hall where an audience sits for performances.

• Option 2 "podium" is a small raised platform for a speaker or conductor.

• Option 3 "hangar" is a large shed in which aircraft are kept.

NOTE

• "Day care" refers to daytime supervision and care of small children (or of the elderly) while family members are at work; the phrase "day care classroom" is common in American usage.

question: Which among the following dance forms of India is associated with Rajasthan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalbelia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kalbelia" is a famous folk dance of Rajasthan, performed by the women of the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community. The swirling black skirts and serpentine movements imitate the movement of a snake. (कालबेलिया — राजस्थान)

• In 2010, Kalbelia songs and dances were inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam — classical dance of Tamil Nadu.

• Odissi — classical dance of Odisha.

• Kathakali — classical dance-drama of Kerala.

NOTE

• Other folk dances of Rajasthan: Ghoomar, Kachhi Ghodi, Chari, Terah Taali, Bhavai and Gair.

question: Bhagat singh and B.K. Dutt threw bomb in the central Legislative Assembly on ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8 April 1929.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw two low-intensity bombs and leaflets in the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi on 8 April 1929, and courted arrest shouting "Inquilab Zindabad". (8 अप्रैल 1929)

• Their aim, in their own words, was "to make the deaf hear" — a protest against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• They belonged to the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA).

• Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged on 23 March 1931 in the Lahore Conspiracy Case (the killing of the police officer Saunders, 1928).

• B. K. Dutt was sentenced to transportation for life.

NOTE

• "Inquilab Zindabad" (Long live the revolution) was coined by Maulana Hasrat Mohani. Bhagat Singh's famous essay is "Why I am an Atheist".

question: 'Freedom in Exile' is the autobiographical book of _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dalai Lama.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Freedom in Exile" (1990) is the autobiography of the 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism, who has lived in exile in India (Dharamshala, Himachal Pradesh) since 1959. (फ्रीडम इन एक्ज़ाइल — दलाई लामा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Jawaharlal Nehru wrote "An Autobiography (Toward Freedom)", "The Discovery of India" and "Glimpses of World History".

• Mahatma Gandhi wrote "The Story of My Experiments with Truth".

• J. B. Kripalani wrote "My Times: An Autobiography".

NOTE

• The 14th Dalai Lama was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989. His other works include "My Land and My People" and "The Art of Happiness".

question: Which of the following is termed as “sericulture”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Commercial rearing of silk worms.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sericulture" is the commercial rearing of silkworms for the production of raw silk. It includes cultivating mulberry, rearing the silkworms and reeling the silk from the cocoons. (रेशम कीट पालन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Viticulture — cultivation of grapes.

• Pomology / horticulture — growing of fruits.

• Pisciculture — breeding of fish.

• India is the second largest producer of silk in the world after China; Karnataka is the leading silk-producing state.

NOTE

• Related terms: apiculture (bee-keeping), floriculture (flowers), olericulture (vegetables), aquaculture (aquatic organisms), sylviculture (forest trees).

• Types of Indian silk: Mulberry, Tasar, Eri and Muga (Muga silk is exclusive to Assam).

question: According to 2011 Census, among the following which state has the lowest sex ratio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, among the options given, Haryana had the lowest sex ratio — 879 females per 1000 males. (हरियाणा — सबसे कम लिंगानुपात)

• The national sex ratio in 2011 was 943 females per 1000 males.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kerala had the highest sex ratio (1084) among states, followed by Puducherry (1037) among UTs.

• Daman and Diu (618) recorded the lowest sex ratio among all States/UTs in 2011.

• Sex ratios in 2011: Bihar 918, Jharkhand 948, Sikkim 890.

NOTE

• The 2011 Census was the 15th national census; its motto was "Our Census, Our Future". Literacy was 74.04% and the decadal growth rate 17.7%.

question: At least how old must be an Indian citizen to be a member of Rajya Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 84 of the Constitution, the minimum age for becoming a member of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is 30 years, while for the Lok Sabha it is 25 years. (राज्यसभा — न्यूनतम आयु 30 वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Rajya Sabha has a maximum strength of 250 members (238 elected from States/UTs + 12 nominated by the President for excellence in literature, science, art and social service).

• It is a permanent house that is never dissolved; one-third of its members retire every two years, each member serving a six-year term.

• The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

NOTE

• Minimum ages: President/Vice-President – 35 years, Governor – 35 years, Rajya Sabha – 30 years, Lok Sabha/Vidhan Sabha – 25 years, Voting – 18 years (61st Amendment, 1988).

question: The product method used to calculate the annual value of goods and services produced is also called ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Value added method.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The product method of estimating national income — which measures the annual value of goods and services produced in an economy — is also known as the "value added method" or the output method. (उत्पाद विधि — मूल्यवर्धित विधि)

• It sums up the value added by every producing enterprise, i.e., the value of output minus the value of intermediate consumption, so that double counting is avoided.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Income method — adds up all factor incomes: rent, wages, interest and profit.

• Expenditure method — adds up total expenditure: C + I + G + (X − M).

• Depreciation is the consumption of fixed capital; it is deducted from Gross value to obtain Net value, and is not a method of national income estimation.

NOTE

• All three methods (product, income and expenditure) must give the same national income, since output = income = expenditure in an economy.

• In India, the National Statistical Office (NSO) under MoSPI estimates national income; the base year currently in use is 2011-12.

question: The most important ruler of the Satavahanas was ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gautamiputra Shri Satakarni.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gautamiputra Satakarni (c. 106–130 CE) is regarded as the greatest and most important ruler of the Satavahana dynasty. He defeated the Saka ruler Nahapana and restored the prestige of the dynasty. (गौतमीपुत्र सातकर्णी)

• His achievements are recorded in the Nasik Prashasti (Nasik cave inscription), issued by his mother Gautami Balashri, which calls him "the destroyer of the Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Simuka was the founder of the Satavahana dynasty.

• Vasisthiputra Pulamavi was the son and successor of Gautamiputra Satakarni; Pulumavi IV was the last important ruler.

• The Satavahanas ruled over the Deccan, with capitals at Pratishthana (Paithan) and Amaravati.

NOTE

• The Satavahanas are known for the Karle and Nasik caves, patronage of Prakrit, and the practice of matronymics (naming rulers after their mothers, e.g., Gautamiputra, Vasisthiputra).

question: Which among the following straits divide Sri Lanka from India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Palk Strait.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Palk Strait" separates India (Tamil Nadu) from Sri Lanka. It connects the Bay of Bengal in the north-east with the Palk Bay and the Gulf of Mannar in the south-west. (पाक जलडमरूमध्य)

• The chain of shoals between Rameswaram (India) and Mannar (Sri Lanka) is called Adam's Bridge / Rama Setu.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Yucatan Strait — between Mexico and Cuba.

• Malacca Strait — between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra (Indonesia); one of the world's busiest shipping lanes.

• Sunda Strait — between the Indonesian islands of Java and Sumatra.

NOTE

• The Palk Strait is named after Robert Palk, a governor of Madras. India's southernmost point on the mainland is Kanyakumari; the southernmost point of Indian territory is Indira Point in the Great Nicobar Island.

question: The Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Award has been instituted in the year 1995. Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was recognized for which dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was the legendary maestro of "Odissi", the classical dance form of Odisha. He is credited with reviving and popularising Odissi in the twentieth century. (ओडिसी — गुरु केलुचरण महापात्र)

• He was honoured with the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan, and also the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Odissi is famous for the tribhanga posture and chowk stance, and draws inspiration from the sculptures of the Konark and Jagannath temples.

• Other noted Odissi exponents: Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi, Protima Bedi and Madhavi Mudgal.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms recognised in India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam). Chhau is a semi-classical/folk martial dance of Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal.

question: Which among the following rivers originates in Maharashtra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Godavari.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Godavari rises at Trimbakeshwar near Nashik in Maharashtra and flows east across the Deccan to empty into the Bay of Bengal. (गोदावरी — त्र्यंबकेश्वर, महाराष्ट्र)

• It is the longest river of peninsular India (about 1465 km) and is often called the "Dakshina Ganga" (Ganga of the South).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Yamuna — originates from the Yamunotri glacier (Uttarakhand).

• Narmada — originates from the Amarkantak plateau (Madhya Pradesh) and flows west into the Arabian Sea.

• Tapi (Tapti) — originates from Multai in Betul district, Madhya Pradesh, and also flows west.

NOTE

• Tributaries of the Godavari: Pravara, Manjira, Purna, Penganga, Wardha, Wainganga, Indravati and Sabari. The Kumbh Mela at Nashik is held on its banks.

question: The Mongols under Genghis Khan invaded Transoxiana in north-east Iran in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1219.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mongols under Genghis Khan (Chingiz Khan) invaded Transoxiana (the region beyond the river Oxus/Amu Darya, in north-east Iran and Central Asia) in 1219. (1219 — चंगेज़ खान का आक्रमण)

• This campaign, launched against the Khwarazmian Empire, brought the Mongols to the frontiers of India during the reign of Iltutmish of the Delhi Sultanate.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Jalaluddin Mangbarni, the fleeing Khwarazmian prince, sought asylum from Iltutmish, who tactfully refused and thereby saved Delhi from a Mongol attack.

• Genghis Khan died in 1227; the Mongol threat continued through the reigns of Balban and Alauddin Khalji.

NOTE

• Alauddin Khalji organised strong defences against Mongol invasions — a permanent standing army, the fort of Siri, and repairs to frontier forts. His general Zafar Khan won notable victories against the Mongols.

question: Which is the largest continent in the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Asia" is the largest continent in the world both by area (about 44.5 million sq km, roughly 30% of the earth's land area) and by population (about 60% of the world's people). (एशिया — सबसे बड़ा महाद्वीप)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Continents by area (largest to smallest): Asia > Africa > North America > South America > Antarctica > Europe > Australia.

• The highest peak on earth, Mount Everest (8848.86 m), and the lowest point on land, the Dead Sea, are both in Asia.

NOTE

• Asia is separated from Europe by the Ural Mountains, the Ural river and the Caspian Sea, and from Africa by the Suez Canal and the Red Sea. Together, Europe and Asia are called Eurasia.

question: Stand Up India scheme aims at supporting entrepreneurship to _______ community of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Scheduled caste.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Stand Up India" scheme, launched on 5 April 2016, facilitates bank loans between Rs. 10 lakh and Rs. 1 crore to at least one Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST) borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch for setting up a greenfield enterprise. (स्टैंड अप इंडिया — अनुसूचित जाति/जनजाति एवं महिला उद्यमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The enterprise may be in manufacturing, services, trading or activities allied to agriculture.

• The scheme is implemented by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, through all scheduled commercial bank branches.

NOTE

• Related schemes: Start-up India (2016) for innovation-driven start-ups, MUDRA Yojana (2015) for micro-units (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun loans) and Stand Up India for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs.

question: Udaipur was founded by ______ after the fall of Chittor to Akbar in 1568.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rana Udai Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rana Udai Singh II of Mewar founded the city of "Udaipur" as his new capital after Akbar captured Chittorgarh in 1568. The city is named after him. (राणा उदय सिंह — उदयपुर)

• Udaipur is famous as the "City of Lakes" and the "Venice of the East" (Lake Pichola, Fateh Sagar Lake).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Maharana Pratap, the hero of the Battle of Haldighati (1576) against Akbar's forces led by Man Singh, was the son of Rana Udai Singh II.

• Sawai Jai Singh II founded Jaipur (1727) and built the Jantar Mantar observatories.

• Raja Bharmal of Amber was the first Rajput ruler to enter into a matrimonial alliance with Akbar.

NOTE

• The Siege of Chittorgarh (1567-68) ended with the fort's fall; Jaimal and Patta are remembered for their heroic defence.

question: Which article of the Indian Constitution provides freedom to manage its own affairs in matters of religion?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 26.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 26 guarantees to every religious denomination the freedom to manage its own affairs in matters of religion — including the right to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes, to own and acquire property, and to administer such property in accordance with law. (अनुच्छेद 26)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 25 — freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion.

• Article 27 — freedom from payment of taxes for the promotion of any particular religion.

• Article 28 — freedom from attending religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained out of State funds.

• Articles 25 to 28 together constitute the Right to Freedom of Religion.

NOTE

• Article 30 gives minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions; Article 5 deals with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution; Article 210 deals with the language to be used in the State Legislature.

question: Who has the power to interpret the constitution of India?
option_3: Both Supreme court and High courts
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both Supreme court and High courts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India, the power to interpret the Constitution rests with the judiciary — both the Supreme Court and the High Courts exercise this power through their writ jurisdiction and the power of judicial review. (सर्वोच्च न्यायालय एवं उच्च न्यायालय दोनों)

• The Supreme Court is the final interpreter of the Constitution, and its decisions are binding on all courts under Article 141.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court and Article 226 empowers the High Courts to issue writs — habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto.

• Judicial review allows the courts to declare a law or executive order unconstitutional (ultra vires).

• The President of India has no power to interpret the Constitution; under Article 143 he may only seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion.

NOTE

• The basic structure doctrine was laid down in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), under which Parliament cannot amend the basic structure of the Constitution.

question: “Ambubachi Mela” is held in which place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guwahati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Ambubachi Mela" is an annual fair held at the Kamakhya Temple on the Nilachal Hills in Guwahati, Assam, generally in June (the month of Ahaar). (अंबुबाची मेला — गुवाहाटी, असम)

• It is associated with the belief in the annual menstruation of the goddess Kamakhya; the temple remains closed for three days and reopens on the fourth amid great celebration.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Kamakhya Temple is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas and a major centre of Tantric worship.

• The Mela draws lakhs of devotees, sadhus and tantriks, and is often called the "Mahakumbh of the East".

NOTE

• Major fairs of India: Kumbh Mela (Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, Nashik), Pushkar Fair (Rajasthan), Sonepur Mela (Bihar), Ambubachi Mela (Assam) and Hemis Festival (Ladakh).

question: Which of the following is an artificial sweetener?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saccharin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Saccharin" (ortho-sulphobenzimide) is the oldest and best known artificial (synthetic) sweetener. It is roughly 550 times sweeter than cane sugar, is not metabolised by the body and gives no calories, so it is used by diabetics and in low-calorie foods. (कृत्रिम मिठास — सैकरीन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Glucose is a natural sugar (monosaccharide) and the body's main source of energy — it is not artificial.

• Lactamase (beta-lactamase) is an enzyme produced by bacteria that destroys penicillin-type antibiotics.

• Sodium benzoate is a food preservative, not a sweetener.

NOTE

• Other artificial sweeteners: aspartame (about 100 times sweeter than sugar, unstable on heating), sucralose (about 600 times), alitame (about 2000 times) and stevia (a natural plant-based sweetener).

question: Which famous Indian sportsman is nicknamed as 'Captain Cool'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahendra Singh Dhoni.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahendra Singh Dhoni, the former Indian cricket captain and wicketkeeper-batsman, is popularly nicknamed "Captain Cool" for his remarkable calmness and composure under pressure. (कैप्टन कूल — महेंद्र सिंह धोनी)

• Under his captaincy India won the ICC World T20 (2007), the ICC Cricket World Cup (2011) and the ICC Champions Trophy (2013) — he is the only captain to win all three ICC white-ball trophies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Major Dhyan Chand — the hockey legend known as "The Wizard/Magician of Hockey"; his birthday, 29 August, is celebrated as National Sports Day.

• Milkha Singh — the sprinter known as the "Flying Sikh".

• Rohit Sharma — known as "Hitman" for his big hitting.

NOTE

• Dhoni received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2007), the Padma Shri (2009) and the Padma Bhushan (2018). He hails from Ranchi, Jharkhand.

question: Practice of “sati” was banned in India in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1829.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The practice of "sati" (the burning of a widow on her husband's funeral pyre) was legally abolished in 1829 by Regulation XVII, passed by the Governor-General Lord William Bentinck. (1829 — सती प्रथा पर प्रतिबंध)

• The reform was strongly supported by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, the founder of the Brahmo Samaj and the "Father of the Indian Renaissance".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other social reforms: the Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856 (championed by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar), the abolition of female infanticide (1795, 1804) and the Age of Consent Act, 1891.

• The modern law on this subject is the Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act, 1987, passed after the Roop Kanwar case.

NOTE

• Lord William Bentinck (Governor-General 1828–1835) also suppressed thuggee (with William Sleeman) and introduced English as the medium of instruction on Macaulay's recommendation (1835).

question: Which of the following material is a conductor of electricity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Silver.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Silver" is a metal and is in fact the best conductor of electricity known, because of the large number of free electrons in its structure. (चाँदी — विद्युत की सर्वोत्तम चालक)

• Order of conductivity: Silver > Copper > Gold > Aluminium.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Glass, mica and ebonite are insulators (bad conductors) — they have no free electrons.

• Mica is widely used as an insulator in electrical appliances (irons, toasters) because it also withstands high temperatures; ebonite is hardened rubber used for insulating handles and battery cases.

• Although silver is the best conductor, copper is normally used in wiring because it is far cheaper.

NOTE

• Materials are classified as conductors (metals, graphite, acidic/salt solutions), insulators (rubber, glass, wood, plastic, mica) and semiconductors (silicon, germanium). Graphite is the only non-metal that conducts electricity well.

question: As of 2022, which Indian musician has the most number of Oscar awards?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A R Rahman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A. R. Rahman has won the most Oscars (Academy Awards) among Indian musicians — two, both in 2009 for the film "Slumdog Millionaire": Best Original Score and Best Original Song ("Jai Ho", shared with the lyricist Gulzar). (ए. आर. रहमान — दो ऑस्कर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Gulzar shared one Oscar (Best Original Song for "Jai Ho") with Rahman; Asha Bhosle and Lata Mangeshkar have not won an Oscar.

• A. R. Rahman, called the "Mozart of Madras", has also won two Grammy Awards, a BAFTA, a Golden Globe, six National Film Awards and the Padma Bhushan (2010).

NOTE

• Other Indian Oscar winners: Bhanu Athaiya (Costume Design, Gandhi, 1983), Satyajit Ray (Honorary Award, 1992), Resul Pookutty (Sound Mixing, Slumdog Millionaire, 2009) and the team of "The Elephant Whisperers" and the song "Naatu Naatu" (2023).

question: Which among the following organs in human body, is most affected by Pneumonia disease?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lungs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pneumonia" is an infection that inflames the air sacs (alveoli) of the lungs, which may fill with fluid or pus, causing cough with phlegm, fever, chills and difficulty in breathing. (निमोनिया — फेफड़े)

• It is commonly caused by the bacterium Streptococcus pneumoniae, and also by viruses and fungi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other lung-related diseases: tuberculosis, asthma, bronchitis, emphysema, silicosis and asbestosis.

• Nephritis affects the kidneys, cystitis the urinary bladder, and myocarditis the heart.

NOTE

• The human lungs are located in the thoracic cavity; the right lung has three lobes and the left lung two lobes. Gaseous exchange takes place across the walls of the alveoli, which number about 300 million.

question: How many field players are in a football team?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A football (soccer) team fields 11 players on the ground at a time — one goalkeeper and ten outfield players arranged as defenders, midfielders and forwards. (फुटबॉल — 11 खिलाड़ी)

• A match is played between two teams of 11 players each over 90 minutes (two halves of 45 minutes).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A football field measures about 100–110 m in length and 64–75 m in width for international matches.

• The international governing body is FIFA (Fédération Internationale de Football Association), founded in 1904, with headquarters in Zurich, Switzerland; the FIFA World Cup is held every four years.

• The Indian football federation is the AIFF (All India Football Federation); national tournaments include the Santosh Trophy and the Durand Cup (Asia's oldest football tournament).

NOTE

• Number of players per side in some games: Cricket 11, Hockey 11, Football 11, Volleyball 6, Basketball 5, Kabaddi 7, Kho-Kho 9 (12 in a team), Water Polo 7.
